verdict.rationale: Working Copy documents that when adding repositories you can 'Link external directory' and pick a folder or Document Package through the Files app, which gives it direct access to repositories in other apps' storage. It also accepts files dragged in from the Files app or other apps, and a directory without a top-level .git subdirectory becomes a new repository, so you can version and work with that content. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that linked external directories work reliably, and documentation of how linked directories stay in sync with the source app and what limitations apply.

support.subject: As a developer, I can access and work with files and repositories from other apps' sandboxes on my device

citations.quote: When adding repositories you tap Link external directory and pick a folder or Document Package in the Files app.
Drag files from your emails, the Files app or any other supporting app to add to your repositories.
If the directory does not contain a .git subdirectory at top-level, Working Copy assumes you want a new repository with all these files added.
